We are interested in connecting with people passionate about Earth science, software development, data analysis, data visualization, and scientific communication.
summary:
ASTRA is an interactive web application developed for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge, addressing “Be An Earth System Trend Detective!”

The project aims to make Earth system data easier to explore and interpret through a collection of focused analytical modules, interactive visualizations, and data-driven workflows.

ASTRA brings together software development, Earth science exploration, data analysis, and visualization in one platform. Its goal is to help users investigate environmental variables, recognize patterns, and explore how Earth system measurements can reveal changes across different regions and over time.

The project was developed as an independent solution for the challenge, with an emphasis on making complex scientific information more accessible through an interactive interface.
details:
ASTRA — Earth System Trend Explorer

ASTRA is an interactive scientific exploration platform that brings multiple Earth, space, and planetary science workflows together in one console. It is designed to help users explore scientific concepts, investigate environmental patterns, interact with analytical tools, and navigate different mission-oriented workbenches through a unified interface.

The platform includes ten workbenches:

  • EarthTrend (CH02): Earth system trend exploration.
  • SAR Explorer (CH06): Synthetic Aperture Radar exploration.
  • Field Shift (CH07): Field-based scientific exploration.
  • FireAtlas (CH09): Fire-related data exploration.
  • LunaNavigator (CH04): Lunar exploration.
  • TerraAnalog (CH10): Planetary analog exploration.
  • MarsExplorer (CH11): Mars exploration.
  • AstroTrainer (CH03): Astronomy learning and exploration.
  • Flame Lab (CH08): Interactive flame-related exploration.
  • MissionForge (CH13): Mission-oriented tools and workflows.

ASTRA brings these different experiences together through a single dashboard, allowing users to navigate between scientific workbenches without needing separate applications.

The project was developed using JavaScript, Node.js, Hono, HTML, CSS, and browser-based technologies. Its architecture combines a web frontend with a backend server to provide an interactive application experience.

The project focuses on making scientific exploration more accessible through a unified interface, interactive workflows, and a collection of tools spanning Earth science, remote sensing, fire investigation, and planetary exploration.

ASTRA aims to demonstrate how multiple scientific workflows can be organized into one accessible and extensible platform.
